title.value: A portrait of the different configurations between digitally-enabled innovations and climate governance
title.justification: The title of the paper captures the essence of its content, focusing on how digital innovations interact with climate governance.
title.quote: A portrait of the different configurations between digitally-enabled innovations and climate governance

extractions.description: This paper explores the intersection of digital innovations and climate governance, examining how these technologies can reshape climate action. It introduces four strategic categories: data mobilization, optimization of existing strategies, incentivizing and automating behavioral change, and enhancing participation and empowerment. Through these strategies, the paper analyzes their potential to transform climate governance using the Earth System Governance framework’s 5 A’s - Architecture, Agency, Adaptiveness, Accountability, and Allocation & Access.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on digitally-enabled innovations in climate governance, directly linking digitalization to climate mitigation efforts.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This work provides a first step towards understanding how digitally-enabled initiatives are contributing to re-imagining climate governance.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on initiatives that impact climate mitigation through digital technologies and strategies that aim to reduce GHG emissions.
primary_category.quote: We identify four broad categories of strategies adopted by these initiatives to help govern climate mitigation.

secondary_categories.justification: The strategies discussed also imply a need for societal adaptation to digital tools for better climate governance.
secondary_categories.quote: Exploring a diversity of digitally-enabled initiatives through the lens of the 5 A’s will enable us to understand how the initiatives in the database address the five key challenges in governance and help explore their potential to re-imagine climate governance.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper discusses the importance of addressing digital divides and supporting digital initiatives in the global south as a part of climate governance.
secondary_categories.quote: This finding highlights potential unconscious biases and/or differences in discursive framing in the context of climate mitigation between the global south and the global north.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus of the paper is on leveraging digital tools and data strategies to monitor and govern climate-related activities effectively.
primary_sub_category.quote: Many initiatives achieve that goal through the use of a variety of digital monitoring and reporting tools, which are intended to feed into verification schemes (e.g. for carbon offset/credit systems).

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper emphasizes the importance of collaboration and knowledge sharing for effective climate governance using digital technologies.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: For societies to transition, they must transform from the 20th century governance model, that embody centralized power structures, top down approaches, and rigid establishments to one that is more iterative, agile, accountable, and interactive with state and non-state actors.

applications.value: Using AI to improve energy efficiency
applications.justification: The paper mentions leveraging AI, a form of digital technology, to optimize energy use as part of climate governance strategies.
applications.quote: Oracle’s Opower utilities software on the other hand uses AI and behavioural science with the objective to increase energy efficiency by providing consumers in-depth information on their energy consumption patterns to encourage behavioural change.

applications.justification: The paper discusses the role of blockchain in creating transparent transactions in carbon offsetting and trading markets.
applications.quote: Initiatives often aim at expanding or improving existing environmental commodity markets through new technologies such as blockchain.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories sufficiently capture the themes of the paper, particularly focusing on Climate Change Mitigation and related governance strategies.
new_primary_category.quote: We identify four broad categories of strategies adopted by these initiatives to help govern climate mitigation.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing sub-categories such as Monitoring, Reporting and Verification align well with the paper's focus on digital governance tools.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Many initiatives achieve that goal through the use of a variety of digital monitoring and reporting tools.
